clue.text: Mutated rat-has view it's due to poison

indicators.note: something mutated has changed its form, so the letters of rat are rearranged

parts.note: to opine is to hold or express a view

explanation.surface: A rat that has mutated sees its condition as the result of poisoning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mutated' rearranges RAT into ATR; 'it's due to' is only a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Atropine is a toxic alkaloid found in deadly nightshade.

clue.text: Is very fond of a great many minerals

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500, a great many
ores are minerals mined for metal

explanation.surface: Someone who loves collecting lots of rock specimens.
explanation.walkthrough: D, the Roman numeral 500, stands for 'a great many'.
explanation.definitionFit: To adore someone is to love them deeply, a strong form of liking.

clue.text: Almost tripped but produced the rent

indicators.note: almost the whole word tripped is used, one letter short of complete

explanation.surface: Someone nearly stumbled but their trousers tore anyway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' drops the first letter T here. A rent is a tear, so to produce one is to have torn something.
explanation.definitionFit: A rent is a tear in cloth, so producing one means having torn it.

clue.text: Visa for dancing pop-stars

indicators.note: dancing suggests the letters of pop-stars moving about into a new order

explanation.surface: Pop stars touring abroad need travel documents to perform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for dancing' rearranges the letters of POP-STARS.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are official travel documents allowing entry to a country, so the setter treats them as near-synonyms.

clue.text: The number single in the North Tyneside area

indicators.note: in places the single letter inside the pair of compass abbreviations

parts.note: NE, the North East of England, is where Tyneside lies
I is the Roman numeral one, a single

explanation.surface: A count of something in the north-east of England.
explanation.walkthrough: Tyneside is the area around Newcastle in North East England, abbreviated NE.
explanation.definitionFit: Nine is a whole number, one more than eight.

clue.text: A detective who could get apartments without money

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the homes go round the money

parts.note: apartments are homes
L stands for pound, as in the old symbol for sterling money

explanation.surface: A sleuth who might manage to find flats without paying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means outside, so HOMES wraps around L. Sherlock Holmes is the fictional detective.
explanation.definitionFit: Sherlock Holmes is the famous fictional sleuth of Baker Street.

clue.text: Test an alternative sort of timber

parts.note: or introduces an alternative
deal is softwood timber such as pine or fir

explanation.surface: Trying out a different kind of wood.
explanation.walkthrough: DEAL is planks of fir or pine, a term familiar in British joinery.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordeal is a severe trial or test of endurance.

clue.text: Hold a man in it, quite wrongly

indicators.note: wrongly means the letters of a man in it are placed out of order

explanation.surface: Detaining a man inside is completely unjust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quite wrongly' rearranges the letters of A MAN IN IT.
explanation.definitionFit: To maintain a position is to keep or sustain it.

clue.text: Make a song about never looking contemptuous

indicators.note: about tells us the singing goes around the word for never

parts.note: to sing is to make a song
ne'er is the poetic contraction of never

explanation.surface: Someone who makes a fuss without ever seeming scornful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make a song about' looks like the idiom for fussing; here SING goes about NE'ER.
explanation.definitionFit: Sneering is showing scorn with a curled lip.

clue.text: Find work modelling that's certainly not agreeable

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work
a model is posing

explanation.surface: Finding work as a model can be quite unpleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'agreeable' here means in agreement, not pleasant.
explanation.definitionFit: To be opposing is to be against something, the reverse of in accord.

clue.text: Plug evil counsel

parts.note: a plug is a short advertisement, an ad
vice is wickedness

explanation.surface: Promoting bad guidance.
explanation.definitionFit: Counsel is guidance or recommendations given to someone.

clue.text: Those going down a point — or several

parts.note: divers descend under water
E is east, a point of the compass

explanation.surface: People going underwater, or many of them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diverse' in its old sense means several or various.
explanation.definitionFit: Diverse can mean various or of many kinds.

clue.text: A number exercise by the river when free

indicators.note: by puts the river beside the other pieces, here in front

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon
M is the Roman numeral 1000
PT is physical training

explanation.surface: Doing some exercises by the riverside in one's free time.
explanation.walkthrough: The Exe is a river in Devon, south-west England, a crossword regular.
explanation.definitionFit: Exempt means released from an obligation that others must meet.

clue.text: The underworld tears about causing chaos

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld and his realm

indicators.note: about signals the letters of tears turned around into a new order

explanation.surface: Hell is weeping over the mayhem it has caused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges TEARS into ASTER. 'tears' could be rips or weeping; it is only fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A disaster is a calamity bringing havoc.

clue.text: Rotter taking on debts? That's odd!

parts.note: a cur is a contemptible fellow
IOUs are written promises of debts

explanation.surface: A scoundrel running up debts is behaving strangely.
explanation.definitionFit: Curious can mean strange or peculiar.

clue.text: Voiced much displeasure as game-birds died

parts.note: grouse are game-birds shot on moors

explanation.surface: Complaints rang out as the shooting season's birds perished.
explanation.definitionFit: To have groused is to have grumbled or complained.

clue.text: Bearing with guys taking one in

indicators.note: taking with in means the word for guys takes the letter inside

parts.note: guys are men
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Composure among men who let someone join.
explanation.definitionFit: Mien is a person's look or manner.

clue.text: Talk and strike back over cut

indicators.note: over in a down clue places one piece above the next
back means the word for strike is read the other way

parts.note: to rap is to strike sharply
to lance is to cut open

explanation.surface: Words exchanged before a counter-blow cuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns RAP into PAR; 'over' sets it above LANCE in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Parlance is a particular way of speaking, an idiom.

clue.text: Elegant furniture designer breaking no hearts

indicators.note: breaking scatters the letters of no hearts into a new order

explanation.surface: A stylish cabinet-maker who doesn't break anyone's heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking' rearranges NO HEARTS. Thomas Sheraton was an 18th-century English furniture designer.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Sheraton gave his name to a refined Georgian style of furniture.

clue.text: Carefree dunderhead getting black look

parts.note: the head of dunder is its first letter D
ebon is a poetic word for black
air is a look or manner

explanation.surface: An idiot with a dark expression is oddly cheerful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dunderhead' reads as fool but splits to the head (first letter) of 'dunder'.
explanation.definitionFit: Debonair means jaunty and light-hearted in manner.

clue.text: Suffer for each motion

indicators.note: in motion the letters of each move about

explanation.surface: Enduring pain with every movement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'motion' rearranges EACH.
explanation.definitionFit: To ache is to feel continuous pain.

clue.text: Used to clean up children in back-street

indicators.note: in places the offspring inside the turned street abbreviation
back means the street abbreviation is turned round

parts.note: issue means offspring

explanation.surface: Wiping kids' faces in an alley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back-street' splits: 'back' is the reversal signal and 'street' the abbreviation it turns to TS; children as 'issue' is the legal word for offspring.
explanation.definitionFit: Paper hankies wipe away mess.

clue.text: Funds for companies

parts.note: reads as cash to start businesses, but describes what firms own and list on a balance sheet

explanation.definitionFit: A company's holdings of value appear on its balance sheet.

clue.text: Where novel and ancient craft can coexist

definitions.text: Where novel and ancient craft can coexist

parts.note: novel means new
Noah's ark is an ancient vessel

explanation.surface: A place where the new and the old ways of building boats live side by side.
explanation.walkthrough: Newark is a town in Nottinghamshire (and New Jersey).
explanation.definitionFit: The town's name combines a word for fresh with a biblical vessel, so it is the place.

clue.text: New style naval force

parts.note: a mode is a style or fashion
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A fresh look for the navy.
explanation.definitionFit: Modern means up to date, recent.

clue.text: Giving a winger encouragement is a bloomer!

parts.note: a lark is a bird, something with wings
a spur is an incentive

explanation.surface: Praising a footballer on the wing turns out to be a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' is a mistake on the surface but a flowering plant here; 'winger' is a bird, not a footballer.
explanation.definitionFit: Larkspur is a flowering garden plant, a delphinium.

clue.text: Jacket for a dance

definitions.meaning: a short open jacket ending above the waist
a Spanish dance in triple time, also Ravel's piece

explanation.surface: A garment suited to dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a short Spanish-style jacket and a Spanish dance share this name.

clue.text: A sportsman down in the dumps

definitions.meaning: at Oxford or Cambridge, someone who has represented the university in a sport

explanation.surface: An athlete who is feeling low.
explanation.walkthrough: At Oxford and Cambridge universities, someone who has competed for the university against the other is awarded a 'Blue'.
explanation.definitionFit: An Oxbridge sporting representative, and also a colour word meaning sad.

clue.text: In days long gone the rabble would lower

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'In days long gone the rabble would lower (6)' for NETHER: no wordplay found giving NETHER from these words; lower is the definition but the rest yields no parse and a search found nothing
annotationWithheld.clue: In days long gone the rabble would lower

clue.text: Prison in which curtailed liberty has brought deep division

indicators.note: in which places the shortened liberty inside the prison word

parts.note: a cage is a place of confinement

indicators.note: curtailed means the tail, the last letter, is cut off

parts.note: leave is permitted freedom, as shore leave

explanation.surface: Imprisonment with restricted freedom has caused a deep rift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'liberty' as leave is a soldier's or sailor's permitted time off; 'curtailed' cuts its final letter to give LEAV.
explanation.definitionFit: A cleavage is a split or sharp division between groups.

clue.text: He's a high-flier, a good man

parts.note: the erne is the sea eagle, a soaring bird
ST is short for saint, a good man

explanation.surface: Praise for an ambitious man of good character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high-flier' suggests a go-getter but is a bird; 'He's' signals a man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernest is a man's first name, so it identifies a male person.

clue.text: Supports family but should be on guard

parts.note: bears means supports, holds up
kin are relatives

explanation.surface: Someone who backs relatives but stays watchful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on guard' means watchful on the surface but here worn by Guards soldiers: the tall fur cap.
explanation.definitionFit: The tall fur hat is worn by British Guards regiments on ceremonial duty.
